subject: Doubts in a simple allometry analysis

messages.author: ef7ac0a24592fcbc
messages.subject: Doubts in a simple allometry analysis
parts:
Hello
I have some experience with Elliptic Fourier analyses in R and, but I have some issues using geomorph. Sorry If this was covered in in the mail group but I couldn’t find it.

I am trying to perform a simple allometry analysis.
>coords_gpagen<-gpagen(A = coords, curves = NULL, surfaces = NULL, PrinAxes = TRUE,max.iter = NULL, ProcD = TRUE, Proj = TRUE, print.progress = TRUE)

>gdf_crudo<-geomorph.data.frame(coords_gpagen, species=mydata$Especie)
>allometry_gdf_crudo<-procD.allometry(coords~Csize,~species,data=gdf_crudo)
I get a significant p for the covariates and for the interaction
> plot(allometry_gdf_crudo, method="PredLine", gp.label = T)

> plot(allometry_gdf_crudo, method = "RegScore", gp.label = T)


  1. Is there an easy way to plot the trajectories for other PCs besides pc1?

  2. Is there a way to extract the slope of the regressions for each PC for each species?(the PredLine plot only shows  PC1)

  3. From the pca (see attachment) I notice a clear positive correlation between size and both PC1 and PC2. I understand the PCs (and slopes) signs are relative, but shouldnt the pca and PredLine signs match? (see attached graphs)

I aso tried with

>procd_gdf_crudo<-procD.lm(coords~Csize*species,data = gdf_crudo)

I get simmilar results but I can’t find the slope for each species in the results.


4)I would also like to compare the slopes but I get a silly error when I tried to do advanced.procD.lm: 

>gdf_crudo<-geomorph.data.frame(coords=coords_gpagen$coords, species=mydata$Especie, Csize=coords_gpagen$Csize)

>PW<-advanced.procD.lm(f1= coords ~ Csize*species, f2= ~Csize+species, iter=999, data = gdf_crudo)

Error in eval(predvars, data, env) : object 'species' not found When I called other functions with species in the formulae I had not any issue. PS: I cant find the quick guide for the 3.0 version (I am working with a cache web version but it is incomplete and poorly formatted) and also the github wiki is not working, is there any other oficial resource? Thanks in advance Santiago Morello

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Doubts in a simple allometry analysis
parts:
Santiago,

 

Please see the help file for procD.allometry and procD.lm.  The output from those functions is far greater than just the anova table (one can extract model coefficients, permuted values, predicted values, etc.). There are also numerous examples of the use of the functions in the help files.

 

For plotting, there are multiple options: PredLine, RegScores, CAC, and equivalent output options from procD.lm.  Again see the help files for the plotting options of these analytical functions.

 

As for directionality of the plots you sent: there is no reason to believe they will coincide in direction. Both plots have some type of data rotated their principal axes, and since the positive and negative ends of such axes are arbitrary, they may not coincide. Also, note that the PC plot is PC1 vs PC2: there is no intuition that directions in this shape-only space would coincide with directions of covariation between shape and size (the second of your plots). A bit more inspection and pondering of the data and the outputs would provide some insight I think.

 

Best,


Dean

The function advanced.procD.lm does contain the fitted values in its S3 output as: $fitted. One may then use these in other exploratory analyses as you were proposing.

As to your first question, I suggest you email me the script and data off-line and I’ll take a look when possible to help you sort this out.

Dean
